final_proof:
Let v_p be the normalized additive p-adic valuation on Q_p, with v_p(p)=1 and v_p(0)=∞. Thus |x|_p=p^{-v_p(x)} for x≠0, the value v_p(x) is an integer for every x∈Q_p^×, and by definition

Z_p={x∈Q_p:|x|_p≤1}={x∈Q_p:v_p(x)≥0}.

First, Z_p is a commutative ring. Indeed, 0,1∈Z_p. If x,y∈Z_p, the ultrametric inequality and multiplicativity of the p-adic norm give

|x−y|_p≤max{|x|_p,|y|_p}≤1

and

|xy|_p=|x|_p|y|_p≤1.

Thus Z_p is closed under subtraction and multiplication and is a subring of Q_p.

We next determine its units. If x∈Z_p and |x|_p=1, then x≠0 and |x^{-1}|_p=|x|_p^{-1}=1. Hence x^{-1}∈Z_p, so x is a unit of Z_p. Conversely, if x is a unit of Z_p, there is a y∈Z_p such that xy=1. Therefore

1=|xy|_p=|x|_p|y|_p.

Both factors on the right are at most 1, so both equal 1; in particular, |x|_p=1. Consequently,

Z_p^×={x∈Z_p:|x|_p=1}.

It follows that the nonunits in Z_p are precisely the elements x with |x|_p<1. We now identify this set. If x≠0, then, because v_p(x) is an integer,

|x|_p<1 ⇔ v_p(x)>0 ⇔ v_p(x)≥1 ⇔ v_p(x/p)≥0 ⇔ x/p∈Z_p.

The equivalence also gives the correct conclusion for x=0, since 0=p·0. Hence

{x∈Z_p:|x|_p<1}=pZ_p.

Thus pZ_p is exactly the set of nonunits of Z_p. It is a proper ideal: it is the principal ideal generated by p∈Z_p, and every element pz with z∈Z_p satisfies |pz|_p≤p^{-1}<1, whereas |1|_p=1, so 1∉pZ_p.

To prove maximality, let I be an ideal with pZ_p properly contained in I. Choose u∈I∖pZ_p. Since pZ_p is the set of nonunits, u is a unit. Therefore 1=u^{-1}u∈I, and I=Z_p. Thus pZ_p is maximal.

Finally, any proper ideal of a ring contains no unit. Hence every proper ideal of Z_p consists entirely of nonunits and is therefore contained in pZ_p. In particular, if M is any maximal ideal of Z_p, then M⊆pZ_p. Since pZ_p is proper, the maximality of M forces M=pZ_p. Therefore pZ_p is the unique maximal ideal of Z_p, proving (b). Since Z_p is a commutative ring with a unique maximal ideal, it is a local ring, proving (a).
